**Colored rooms.** A room's own light now takes the color of the lamps and
glowing textures that light it, the way the mapper meant it. The floor right
under a red lamp is the reddest spot and the color fades out from there,
instead of a grey patch under the lamp with red around it (the monitor boxes
in E1M1 were the plainest case). Monsters, items and your weapon take the same
tint as the floor they stand on. White lights look as before.

**Glowing textures light the rooms they are in.** Nearby light panels and
glowing floors of one color are combined into one light, and that light could
land inside a wall between two rooms, so neither room got it. About 7% of the
glowing textures in DOOM and DOOM II were affected, and some maps lost most of
their panel light: E4M5 about three quarters, E3M7 and E4M9 over half,
DOOM II MAP03 nearly half. Lights now only combine with ones they can see.

**Light panels shine forward.** Wall panels and computer screens now light only
what is in front of them, fading out toward their own wall, so their light no
longer stops in hard lines at corners and behind free-standing screens. The
wall around a panel keeps its glow.

**Other changes**

- Lamp light no longer stays capped at a sector's starting brightness after
  flickering lights or switches change it.
- A light panel partly hidden behind a ledge or low opening now lets part of
  its light through instead of none.
